summary: Read the Lap-Lab idea (version 1) and wrote a minimal 11-section prototype specification to .surety/spec/spec.md. The idea's six lessons plus final exercise do not fit 5 objectives within the prototype budget, so scope is reduced to three lessons (acceleration/mass, braking point, corner grip) with five requirements: lesson setup and map, synchronized animated telemetry, coherent physics with unsuccessful runs, results and history, and prediction/interpretation feedback. The exit, wing and sensor lessons and the final exercise are listed in left_out. The idea's 'no server' environment is satisfied by a static localhost server, as recorded in assumptions.

brief.app: Lap-Lab is a desktop browser game where you act as a race engineer: you change one variable on one section of a fictional circuit and use animated telemetry to explain what happened.
brief.for: Adults with general technical curiosity and no racing expertise, playing for fun.
brief.experience: Pick a lesson, see the active section highlighted on a dark race-engineering console, predict, adjust one control, watch the car and reference ghost run while graphs grow, then inspect the evidence and answer what happened and why.
included: A fictional, believable circuit with a full map and a detailed view of the highlighted active section.
Three lessons: acceleration on a straight (mass), finding the braking point (braking start), using corner grip (target corner speed).
Exactly one adjustable variable per lesson, with reference value and a visible list of fixed conditions.
Animated car with reference ghost, and distance-based telemetry graphs that draw progressively.
Synchronized play, pause, replay, scrubber, graph cursor, numeric readouts and keyboard graph inspection.
Tire grip-demand indicator for the braking and corner lessons.
Result panel with section time, delta, key metric and valid/unsuccessful/pending status.
In-session experiment history that can be revisited.
Multiple-choice prediction and interpretation questions with evidence-based feedback and a lesson completion state.
objectives: R1: On load the player sees the lesson question, the highlighted active section on the full circuit map, the single adjustable control with its fixed conditions, and how to start.
R2: Running an experiment animates the car and reference ghost while distance-based telemetry grows, with car, cursor, readouts, pause, replay and scrubber always in sync.
R3: Changing the variable produces a deterministic, coherent change in behaviour and time, and too-late braking or infeasible corner speeds are marked unsuccessful rather than fast.
R4: Each run shows section time, delta to reference, key metric and status, and earlier runs in the session can be revisited from a history list.
R5: Each lesson asks a multiple-choice prediction and interpretation question and gives feedback that cites the adjustment, result, location and physical reason, ending in a visible completion state.
mocked: Vehicle behaviour comes from a simplified illustrative point-mass model with a friction-circle grip limit, not a validated vehicle dynamics simulation.
All telemetry is generated by the model; none of it is recorded data.
left_out: Lesson 4: building corner exit speed (throttle application point).
Lesson 5: balancing drag and downforce (wing setting), including aerodynamic force arrows.
Lesson 6: reading a questionable signal (sensor noise, raw vs smoothed view, withheld explanation).
The integrated final exercise on the complete circuit, including whole-lap vs section results.
Inspecting a run by clicking a location on the track section (inspection is via graph and scrubber).
Additional discoverable signals beyond each lesson's core set.
assumptions: The idea's 'no server' requirement is met by a plain static file server on localhost with all logic running in the browser.
Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with SVG or Canvas rendering is acceptable.
Illustrative distances, masses, speeds and times may be chosen freely as long as they are coherent.
Reviewers use a current desktop Chromium- or Firefox-based browser at 1280x800 or larger.
limitations: Only three of the six lessons are present, and there is no final exercise.
Physics omit weight transfer, tire temperature, gearing detail and yaw dynamics.
Infeasible runs stop or flag at the limit rather than showing a spin animation.
Accessibility covers keyboard graph inspection, focus states and non-colour cues, but has not been formally audited.
Visual polish is judged by reviewers and has no automated check.
constraints: Desktop only; tablets and phones are not supported.
Nothing persists between visits; no accounts, analytics or answer collection.
Predictions and interpretations are multiple choice only.
The circuit is fictional and must not copy or name a real track.
Exactly one adjustable variable per experimental run, with all other conditions held fixed.
No manual driving, real telemetry, import/export, multiplayer, leaderboards, sound or localization.
Professional dark motorsport-console presentation, and no colour-only distinctions.
Success is judged by human reviewers on the idea's review dimensions.
